content.comment_body: Hello, I'm encountering an issue with communication between [product_name] [version_no] and [product_name] (firmware [version_no]) over ethernet. The system functioned properly at our facility, but after installation onsite, we receive an error stating: "Secure connection to [product_name] [version_no] or higher cannot be established; verification of certificate failed." The error LED on the [product_name] module is lit red. A ping test from [product_name] to [product_name] is successful and time synchronization appears to function. The certificate from [product_name] is received by the [product_name] module, but the secure connection is not established (no diagnostic message shown), and monitoring does not work (digital flags are shown in red). The IP addresses are: [product_name]: 192.168.0.1; [product_name]: 192.168.0.3. Thank you in advance.
Please submit a support request for assistance.
I've already submitted a support request alongside this topic, but I'm hoping someone can provide a quick solution.

Hi, I'm not highly experienced with using [product_name] together with [product_name], but based on your screenshot, from line 7 onward your date and time settings seem incorrect. Adjusting the date and time may resolve the issue with securing the connection.

Thank you for your suggestion. Time synchronization is active on the [product_name] module and is sourced from the mobile wireless network. It then sends the updated time to [product_name]. According to line 8 of the diagnostic buffer, time synchronization has succeeded. When there is a discrepancy, the time visibly updates on the [product_name] display. So, unfortunately, time synchronization does not appear to be the cause.
Line 4 indicates that the connection to [product_name] [version_no] failed due to base module certificate verification failure.
Were you able to resolve the issue?
I'm facing the same problem with the latest firmware on both [product_name] [version_no] and [product_name]. Is it necessary to load a different certificate into the [product_name] to resolve this?
Hi, you initially mentioned that you have [product_name] [version_no], but IXOS identifies [product_name] [version_no]. Have you checked your settings and made sure they're correct?

analysis.insight_summary: Users are experiencing difficulty establishing secure communication between [product_name] [version_no] and [product_name] after onsite deployment, despite successful factory testing. The main obstacle is certificate verification failure which disrupts secure connectivity and monitoring capabilities. Troubleshooting measures like time synchronization and verification of settings have not fixed the certificate-related problem, resulting in ongoing system downtime and confusion.
analysis.user_expectations: Users are seeking a stable and straightforward secure connection between [product_name] and [product_name] modules, anticipating easy certificate management to deliver reliable system communication and monitoring.
